I'm 55, been farming these 129 mu in Quzhou for 40 years now. Finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and the extension notices they put up at the village office, but honestly, I mostly go by what I've seen with my own eyes and what the experienced farmers around here do. My wife works part-time at the garment factory in town, so day-to-day it's mostly me on the land. With only two of us at home, I have to hire seasonal labor for planting, spraying, and harvesting—can't run 129 mu on family labor alone.

My main system is still wheat-maize double cropping on 105 mu. That's the backbone of the farm. The wheat went in last October with a hybrid variety—about 18 kg of seed per mu. I put down base fertilizer in the fall: compound fertilizer plus some urea, totaling about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu for the whole wheat season. Now that spring is here, I'll topdress with urea at jointing—another 8 kg of nitrogen per mu or so. I irrigate three times for wheat: green-up in March, jointing in April, and grain-filling in May. The pumping costs money, but I learned back in 2012 that skimping on water costs you more at harvest. I'd rather waste a bit on extra fertilizer or water than risk a bad year. I'm expecting around 480 kg per mu if the weather holds.

The summer maize goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. Turnaround is tight—sometimes only five or six days. I hire a custom planter because there's no way to do 105 mu by hand in that window. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea at the big trumpet stage, about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu total. Two irrigations: one if it's dry at planting, and one at flowering in August. Hoping for about 520 kg per mu.

I've got 15 mu of cotton this year. Cotton is labor-heavy, especially the picking, but lint prices have been decent and the neighbor down the road did well with it last year. I plant in mid-April. I split the fertilizer three times—base, flowering, and boll stage—about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu total. Two irrigations, and I keep insecticide ready for bollworm; that's the pest that'll ruin you if you're not watching. I'm targeting 280 kg of lint per mu, but cotton's always a bit of a gamble.

The remaining 9 mu is millet. Partly for our own household—we like millet porridge in winter—and partly to sell at the county market. It's low-risk, low-input. I put down compound fertilizer once at planting, about 10 kg of nitrogen per mu, and irrigate maybe once if the summer is really dry. Expecting around 220 kg per mu.

Labor is my biggest headache. I hire workers for wheat harvest, maize planting, and cotton picking. For cotton, I pay pickers by the kilo. It adds up, but I have no choice. Total input costs this year—seed, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation electricity, and hired labor—will run me about 72,000 yuan. That's a lot of cash to put out before harvest, but I've been at this long enough to know that cutting corners loses you money in the end.
